---
title: "Research"
description: "Statistical foundations for AI-generated ground truth and LLM evaluation."
---

My research asks when an LLM evaluation can be trusted, when the labels, judges, and budgets behind it are imperfect. All of it uses public datasets.

## Current topics

- **AI-generated ground truth.** When several LLMs label the data, which label errors actually change which model wins, and which are harmless.
- **Evaluation budgets.** Whether to spend a fixed budget on more test items, more human labels, or more reruns, by separating human label disagreement from model non-determinism.
- **Guarantees for evaluation.** Statistical certificates that a model comparison still holds when the labels behind it are imperfect.

LLM-as-a-judge is a recurring thread.
